scope: v1 core + v2 breadth/oversold alerts and audio edition + v3 policy section and mortgage rate + v4 Owen's Alphabet Soup (daily grounded lesson, client-owned pointer) + v5 spoken rates readout (10-year, 30-year mortgage, VIX, each with its why), the Monday policy digest, cross-bucket audio dedupe, and self-healing lesson audio + v6 leveraged ETF pulse (SOXL/SPXL/TQQQ: RSI-14 and the 1-month closing band, page and audio) + v7 watchlist (any Yahoo ticker via watchlist.txt, a buy/trim/hold action classified once and used by both the card colour and the audio, audio limited to the actionable tickers, missing symbols named on the page)
note: Project docs/ is the GitHub Pages web root (PWA), not documentation. Dev docs live in documentation/.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.summary: System overview, data flow, modules, key design decisions (incl. the monitors and their fail-closed guards, the deterministic no-model watchlist section, the buy/trim/hold action classified once and shared by the card and both voices, the policy-section accuracy guarantees, the no-year static policy calendar, and why the Alphabet Soup lesson pointer is client-side), briefing.json and lessons.json schemas, CLI entry points.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.summary: External services (Yahoo Finance for both the headline numbers and the watchlist pulse, Gemini, ntfy, RSS, Federal Register, Utah Legislature, Freddie Mac PMMS, the Wikipedia action API behind Owen's Alphabet Soup, the TradingView scanner behind breadth, GitHub Pages/Actions, v2 Twelve Data), usage, invocation sites, per-build request budgets, env var names, the probed-dead source list, and the static POLICY_CALENDAR that stands in for the annual announcements no feed publishes.

docs.title: Operations
docs.summary: Scheduling and DST, one-time deployment (secret/var name mapping), runtime, monitoring (every alarm path: six notify.py publishers plus five workflow-level ntfy curls, incl. the watchlist crossing push and the guard-triggers trip), run-state keys and their writers (and why the lesson pointer is deliberately not one), failure modes and recovery per section (incl. the per-ticker fail-close on the watchlist pulse and why it is not in markets_ok), regression tests and their negative controls (incl. the narration mirror's seven controls and the empty-fixture trap), cost.
